title: Homan Mandates Body Cameras at All ICE Vehicle Stops After Dual Fatal Shootings
excerpt: Border Czar Tom Homan announced that at least one body camera must be active during every ICE vehicle stop, following the fatal shootings in Houston and Maine that lacked any body camera footage despite a $20 million congressional appropriation.
content:
On July 19, 2026, White House Border Czar Tom Homan announced on Fox News that ICE acting director had directed all officers to wear at least one body camera during vehicle stops. The announcement came after two fatal traffic-stop shootings in less than a week and mounting congressional pressure.

The new policy acknowledged implicitly that the body camera program that DHS had pledged to 'rapidly deploy' nationwide in February 2026 had not been completed despite $20 million in congressional funding. DHS blamed a partial government shutdown earlier in 2026 for interrupting the procurement process. Homan stated that cameras had been purchased and that ICE was 'training the trainer' to deploy them.

  • Homan said he supported body cameras because 'they exonerate more law enforcement than they convict,' and wanted the public to see what officers saw when force was used.
  • The new body camera mandate applied specifically to vehicle stops; officers would be required to have cameras activated for the duration of such stops.
  • DHS expected full nationwide body camera coverage across all ICE field offices within approximately 60 days.
  • 39 senators — including Independent Angus King of Maine and 38 Democrats — had written to DHS Secretary Mullin the same day demanding ICE reforms, including mandatory body cameras, visible identification, and no masks during operations.
